 a. “And indeed Mexico City is not unlike any other large place for when Sunday arrives Chapultepec Park is filled with excursionists.”
Fountain, pedestrian traffic, canoes, fountain in lake.

Gate - castle from patio - people on long veranda - thatched hut by water - house - man poling boat.
“Mexico’s most beautiful city was named after the old Moorish capital Wadal-il-harah.”
City from high point.
“No other city in Mexico can better exemplify the progress of this country than Guadalajara. From a sleepy village it has risen to a busy industrial city of over 135,000 population. It is also an important railroad center.”
Railroad station - crowds.
“On the main plaza one meets with a pleasant mannered and light-hearted people, but no wonder, for the state of Jalisco, of which Guadalajara is the capital, was settled by Spanish aristocracy in 1530.”
Street scenes.
“The principle streets are lined with handsome white stone buildings in which are located shops of every description, banks and commercial agencies. San Francisco is the main street.”
Street from above, from in street, streetcar, pedestrian traffic - building.
“Like castles in the air are Guadalajara’s beautiful homes - for the city situated at an altitude of 5,000 feet assures its population of an average climate of 70 degrees the year round.”
Tree-lined streets, homes. 
“The National Theater.” [Mexico City]
The building, automobile, pedestrian, horse-drawn vehicle traffic.
“The National Pawn Shop and the Plaza de Constitucion, two of Mexico City’s landmarks.”
“A short distance away from the Mexican metropolis looms the church of the sacred city of Mexico, Guadalupe.”
Mexican children on dirt road, church in background - views of church. 
“At San Juan Teotihuacan are the pyramids resembling in many ways their Egyptian counterparts.”
Views of pyramids - man sitting on huge gargoyle - museum interior, ancient Indian stone carvings. 
“Xochimilco Indians paddle along this canal in their clumsy crafts among the flower burdened islands which were once floating.” 
“The Alameda is a handsome subtropical park which is bathed daily in plenty of sunshine and beautiful music.” 
“The Benito Juarez monument was erected in 1910 to commemorate the 100th anniversary of Mexican independence.” 
“The Chamber of Deputies where President Obregon took his oath of office on December 1, 1920.” 
“The old Jockey Club is now a popular American restaurant.”
Street, traffic. 
“Ministry de Comunicaciones, building of Public Works.” [1920]

Meat placed in pan and put into oven - industrial building complex. [1920]

record.scopeAndContentNote:
The original catalog description provided by the Ford Motor Company reads as follows:

 a. “Montcalm, Ethan Allen, Washington, Franklin and others who have made American history have passed through the gateway of this old fort.”
Tourists enter stone ruin through arched opening - sign. List of great men who have entered. 
“Every effort is made to fit each boy in his proper place - as in the case of the printer.”
Print shop - boys operate press, set type.
“With surprising skill these boys surpass their more fortunate rivals.”
Wood shop, boy making toy lawn swing - boy making child’s bench. 
“All the work-shoes for the school are of their own making.”
Cobbler shop - boy making shoes - buffing with machinery. [1918]
b. “A very old and well-preserved specimen of Spanish architecture on Saint Francis St. Why is the street so narrow?”
Automobile, bicycle, pedestrian traffic. 
“Here in the midst of Spanish surroundings are the remains of a Huguenot cemetery. Who were the Huguenots?”
“One of the first chapels in America.”
“The old fort called San Marco Castle; these are only desolate cold walls, but if stones could talk, what wonderful stories they might tell.”
Views of the fort, tourists. 
“The ramparts.” 
“The main tower.”
“The narrowed street of St. Augustine.”
“The Spanish were great explorers...San Miguel Church, the oldest church in the United States.”
“This old adobe house was built by Pueblo Indians long before the Spaniards came. It is the oldest dwelling in America.” 
“Four hundred years ago Santa Fe was made the capital of the kingdom of New Mexico. This building was reconstructed from an old Indian building and was the palace of the governors.”
Large one-story adobe building - monument - (‘Samuel Champlain with two companions and sixty Indians entered this lake in canoes in 1609. Lake bears his name’ written on film). 
“Columbus is given the credit for the discovery of the New World, but some evidences seem to indicate Leif Ericson touched the shore of America in 1000 A.D.”
Monument. 
“The Old Stone Mill on Round Tower in Newport. Its origin is unknown but it was probably built by the Norsemen.”
“The early Spanish settlements shown on a map of Florida.” 
“Ponce de Leon landed here.” 
“He thought this was the ‘Fountain of Youth.’”
Tourist dips water from spring enclosed by building. 
“The sword he buried.”
“In 1565 Pedro Menedez de Avitas touched these shores and landed where St. Augustine now stands. He established the first permanent settlement.”
Panorama of St. Augustine. 
“Beyond these gates is St. Augustine. In the early days there were no other entrances.”
Automobiles driven through gate.
“While this may not actually be the ‘oldest house in the United States,’ it is a curious, old structure erected in 1590.”
Sign in window, ‘The Oldest House in the United States, Containing $75,000 Collection of Antiques’ - the house - statue in garden.
“An old Spanish building built in 1591. It was the Spanish governor’s palace but is now the United States post office.” [1918]
c. “The carding machine combs and straightens the cotton fibers.”
“Heaping cotton and wool in layers preparatory to mixing.”
“A couple of good mixers mix things up for the final carding.”
Old man with arms full of mixture.
“Carding combs and straightens the fibers. What’s left is called ‘roving,’ the basis of yarn.” [1918]
d. “A bountiful supply of good things to eat may be obtained throughout the year. Tropical fruits, such as the banana, thrive in certain altitudes about Guadalajara.”
Street, tropical trees. 
“Rest assured that when there is an American colony there also will be found a Country Club.”
“Although there are few important rivers and lakes in Mexico many good places to bathe may be found just the same.”
Pools.
“Independence monument.”
“The Hospicio, instead of being used as a hospital, is an asylum for the poor of all ages.”
Building, traffic, automobile and pedestrian - horseback riders in rocky desert canyon. 
“Natures Echo -- One Last Look.” “Produced by Ford Motor Co.”
Man beside tent looks out over lake; cloud shrouded mountain. [1918]
e. Little Bo Peep
“Little Bo Peep she lost her sheep --”
Worker shears sheep.
“This river supplies about sixty-five percent of the motive power for running these woolen mills.”
River, mill.
“Unpacking a bale of Marino wool which is imported from Australia.” 
“Wool is sorted into grades according to textures.” 
“It is then fed into a washing machine containing strong solution of scouring chemicals.” 
“A fifty percent shrinkage results from scouring received.”
Machinery in operation.
“Raw cotton is placed in dusters to loosen fibers and eliminate dirt.” 
“The lapping machine partially straightens the fibers and removes other impurities.”
Worker places fibers in hopper of a machine, they come out as batting. [1918]

record.scopeAndContentNote: Reel 1: Introductory scroll titles give history and organization. Coast Guard Cutter underway. Storm breaks over sea wall. Disabled vessel at sea. Men at work on deck of Coast Guard cutter towing disabled vessel in heavy storm. Coast Guard stations on the Atlantic shoreline. Ship wrecked on reef. Coast Guard land force shoots line from shore to wrecked vessel and sets up breeches buoy. Shipwreck victims brought to shore by means of breeches buoy. Ship on fire at sea. Cutter underway. Power lifeboat at sea. Burning tanker at sea. Ship on reef. Lifeboat comes to shore. Warship at sea. Camouflaged war transports. Map showing Coast Guard areas. Coast Guard Depot at Curtis Bay, Maryland. Footage: 841 feet.  Reel 2: Coast Guard station at Miami, Florida. Airplane hangar. Planes and crew on inspection. Planes take off. Amphibian plane comes up the runway out of the water. Machine gun on plane. Land plane takes off. Cape May station in New Jersey. Planes on land and in the air. Freighter at sea. Radio room at Coast Guard station. Message is received and given to pilot. Coast Guard plane takes off. Plane flies low over ship at sea and continues on its journey. Ship at sea. Plane lands near freighter. Lifeboat is lowered from vessel and is rowed to plane. Helpless person is transferred from lifeboat to plane and plane takes off. Plane lands at station, pulls up on runway, and helpless person is lifted out. Doctor examines person and orders immediate removal. Person on stretcher is put into ambulance and vehicle pulls away. Footage: 782 feet.  Reel 3: Titled "The Academy." The Academy campus from the air. Cadets on parade. Bugler sounds breakfast call. Breakfast formation. Cadets march into mess hall. Cadets seated at mess. Radio class. The direction finder. The engineering laboratory. Students at work on engine. The ordnance class. Infantry drill. Cadets present arms. Football game. Two students at study desks. Cadets boardCoast Guard cutter for three months summer cruise. Cutter at sea. Marksmanship training at Quantico, Va. Instruction classes onboard cutter. Cadets fire three-inch gun in record time. The five-inch gun in operation. Targets show hits made. Cutter arrives at dock. Cadets leave cutter. Graduation at the Coast Guard Academy. Cadets are presented with diplomas by the Assistant Secretary of the Treasury. Cadets stand and sing Academy song. Footage: 980 feet.  Reel 4: Titled "Service Afloat." Cutter at sea. The captain on the bridge. Radio room. New York City skyline from the river. Medical officers board Coast Guard tug in New York harbor. Tug meets liner outside of harbor and officers board liner. Liner comes in. Small boats at college crew race. Shells underway. Patrol boat on duty. Yachts underway. The United States fleet on parade. Small vessels at sea. Cutter pulls alongside small boat. Direction finder on cutter. Disabled tug is sighted at sea. Deck of cutter is cleared for action. Coast during storm. Coast Guard power lifeboat gets underway. Barges founder off the coast. Hurricane on Florida coast. Wreckage caused by the hurricane. Coast Guard on duty. The Mississippi River in flood. Coast Guard boats containing refugees land their cargoes on high ground. Man is rescued from top of floating house. Boat filled with livestock. Cutter breaks way through ice. Cutter on sea patrol. Derelict is sighted. Small boat puts out toward derelict, mine is planted under wreckage, small boat pulls away and derelict is blown up. Disabled freighter at sea. Cutter underway. Footage: 950 feet. Reel 5: Training school at Fort Trumbell, Connecticut. Different types of seamen's knots. Signal drill. Radio instruction. Receiving and sending apparatus. Rifle practice. Captain of cutter on lookout. Captain throws a life preserver overboard. Men climb into lifeboat. Boat is lowered and is rowed to life preserver. Preserver is hooked and pulled into boat.Instructions in artificial respiration. Signal drill at sea. Sailors shine brass on cutter. The galley. Men at mess. Open deck barber shop. Men dive from deck of cutter into ocean. The gym onboard a cutter. Men play games on deck. Patrol boat underway. Cutter pickets smuggler. Cutter chases smuggler. Guardsmen board smuggling vessel. Seal patrol. Seals on island. Icebergs at sea. Coast Guardsmen shoot icebergs from cutter. The Morro Castle burns at sea. A 75 foot patrol boat fights to reach the burning vessel. Lifeboat is launched from shore in an attempt to reach the burning vessel. Surfboat is rushed along shore form neighboring Coast Guard station. Crowd watches as Coast Guardsmen aid victims in their efforts to reach shore. The remains of the charred vessel aground at Asbury Park, N.J. Footage: 1,025 feet.  Reel 6: Titled "Service Ashore." Coast Guard station. Boat comes down runway. Boat is rowed away. Map of Coast Guard stations and houses of refuge along the coasts. Wrecked schooner. Liner on reef. Lighthouse. Freighter aground. Ship aground on beach. Rescues made by Coast Guard. Stations on Long Island. Long Island coasts and New Jersey sands. Ocean resorts. Crowded resorts. Yachts and other pleasure craft at sea. Coast Guard station. Power lifeboat comes down the runway. Boat underway. Wrecked vessel. Jones Beach, N.Y. Swimming race. Slow motion diving. Big liner underway. Jones Beach Coast Guard station. Lifeboat is carried down to the beach. Car carries boat on trailer down highway to point desired and runs it out on the beach. Hurricane wreckage. Footage: 1,029.  Reel 7: Yacht grounded on the beach. Coast Guard tractor brings surfboat down to beach. Boat puts out to sea carrying small line. Tug out from the beach. Boat pulls alongside tug and returns to beach. The small line is pulled back from the tug and a still larger one enables the big towing hawser to be hauled in. Ropes are placed around the hull of the yacht andtied to the hawser. The signal is given. The tug pulls off and the yacht slides over the sands into the water. Man walks along shore and sees half-drowned man. He pulls him out of the water and immediately begins to administer artificial respiration treatment. The lookout in the station tower spots the find and aid is rushed out to the beach. Man is revived and is carried away. Night patrolman on duty. He punches a clock at the end of his beat with a key attached to a post. He holds up flare. Coast Guard boat pulls out for race. Surfboat race. Upset race. Footage: 747 feet.  Reel 8: Apparatus for the breeches buoy is brought out. The line is set up and the gun shot. The line is caught by other men in mast some distance away. Hawser is tugged up to the mast and the breeches buoy set up. Men come down via breeches buoy. Snapping device is attached to hawser and pulled out to the mast. Hawser is snapped at mast and is pulled in. Vessel on reef. Victims rescued via breeches buoy. Ship on rocks. Power lifeboat at sea. Breeches buoy set up on rocks. Victims are saved. Coast Guard cutter underway. Coast Guard stations, patrol boats and fast chasers. Small vessels at sea. Fishing boats. Coast Guardsmen boarding vessel. Cutter on the chase. Gun is shot at retreating vessel. Coast Guardsmen and boats in action.
